# Real EEG feasibility test — protocol fixed before model results

Dataset: Shin et al., 2018, dataset A (n-back), participant VP001 selected by identifier, not performance. Source: https://doc.ml.tu-berlin.de/simultaneous_EEG_NIRS/. Preserve the original archive/headers/markers and record hashes. No synthetic samples, merged people, or transferred synthetic weights.

## Questions

1. Does the existing frontal-theta stretch rule identify sustained task periods above the session's rest baseline? Task periods are behavioral proxies, not ground-truth neural stretches. Report interval overlap, task/rest score separation, and off-task flags, including failure.
2. Can an evoked-response classifier rank target versus non-target trials on unseen blocks from the same session? Stimulus markers supply timing for this positive control. This does not by itself demonstrate marker-free burst detection.
3. In a separate continuous scan, does the same frozen ERP model retrieve target-associated candidate times without receiving stimulus timestamps? Compare full scan and detected-stretch onset gates at a fixed review budget. Ground truth is target timing, not direct evidence that every trial contains a visible P300.

## Split and acquisition audit

Inspect metadata/markers before scoring. Treat each raw n-back file/session separately. Within each session use the first two occurrences of each n-back level for calibration and the final occurrence for held-out evaluation. Do not train on one session and report another as calibrated. Expected: three repetitions each of 0-, 2-, and 3-back, with 20 stimuli per 40-second task block. If actual markers disagree, resolve against source metadata before training; document deviations rather than silently dropping blocks.

Preserve TP9 acquisition reference, record header filter information, explicitly map FP1→Fp1, FP2→Fp2, AFF5→AFF5h, AFF6→AFF6h. Use all 28 EEG channels for ERP; keep HEOG/VEOG separate for artifact audit. No silently missing channels. Resample continuous blocks from the raw sampling rate to 200 Hz with anti-alias filtering and preserve event seconds. Filter each independent block with its surrounding rest context; no overlapping samples between block groups.

## Stretch branch

Use the existing 4–8 Hz frontal log-power rule: centered 2 s power window; calibration-rest median/MAD; entry z=3, release z=1.5, minimum duration 3 s; ±3 s onset gate. Frontal set: Fp1, Fp2, AFF5h, AFF6h, AFz, F1, F2, available explicitly. No tuning this rule on held-out blocks. Report quality-rejected coverage separately. Rest used for baseline must exclude instructions, stimuli, and boundaries. Evaluate each of 0-/2-/3-back as task vs rest; also report the direction of theta differences between workload levels descriptively.

## ERP branch

Use 2-/3-back target/non-target markers. Exclude 0-back from target discrimination because the documented marker scheme does not provide an equivalent negative class. Epoch −0.1 to +1.0 s relative to stimulus; baseline correct using pre-stimulus samples; continuous 1–30 Hz fourth-order Butterworth zero-phase filtering. Reject gross amplitude/step/flatline artifacts, using fixed limits and a context guard; report rejected counts by class and block. Show HEOG/VEOG activity alongside EEG ERP averages to expose ocular confounding; no claim of complete artifact removal.

Framework classifier: xDAWN with 3 target-class filters + prototype covariance (Ledoit–Wolf), affine-invariant tangent reference, StandardScaler, class-balanced L2 logistic regression. Tune C over [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10] inside calibration using block-group CV; every learned transform refits in each fold. Compare a simple baseline of channel mean amplitudes over five fixed 200 ms post-stimulus bins with the same scaler/classifier/C search. Inner folds must contain both classes. No choice between models or retuning based on held-out scores.

Report held-out AUROC, average precision and class-prevalence baseline, balanced accuracy at decision margin zero, and per-block counts. Small participant/session results are feasibility checks, not population accuracy. Do not count neighboring windows as independent evidence or claim statistical significance from this sample.

## Continuous retrieval

Use the trained ERP branch on a 100 ms candidate-onset grid with the same epoch/baseline and preprocessing. The scanner receives samples only; annotations are used later for evaluation. Exclude artifact/edge windows. Rank by decision margin, accept nonnegative margin, suppress candidates within 1.5 s, return up to five candidates per held-out block (same budget for all/onset search). Match target stimulus timestamps one-to-one within ±0.5 s of proposed onset. Score off-task/rest and non-target candidates as unmatched, while labeling this specifically a target-retrieval proxy rather than a universal false cognitive-event rate. Report accessible target recall and valid-grid coverage for the onset gate. Export stretches and ERP candidates separately with replayed_eeg provenance, and show average target/non-target waveforms for context.

Any change required by file/marker audit or an implementation bug will be logged below before results are interpreted. Performance-driven changes require a new holdout and are outside this first pass.

## Marker audit adjustment (before scoring)

The original VP001 markers contain 20 events per block, but actual inter-stimulus intervals are about 2.2 s, not exactly 2 s. Therefore do not impose nominal 40 s blocks or regenerate stimulus times. Use recorded task onset, recorded individual stimulus times, and estimate task end as the last stimulus plus that block's median inter-stimulus interval. This last endpoint is an estimate because no explicit stop marker is present.

Give each task block its own nonoverlapping slice from 10 s before its block marker to 10 s after estimated task end. Use rest segments from −8 to −4 s before onset and +4 to +8 s after estimated task end for calibration; exclude task boundaries/instructions. Assert that raw sample intervals do not overlap between groups. The first six blocks contain two occurrences of each condition and precede the held-out final three blocks. Verify this independently in every run. No weights transfer between the three n-back sessions.

The original header records mixed acquisition low-pass settings (250 Hz on the first 24 channels, 1000 Hz on the last six, at 1000 Hz sampling), low-cut time constant 10 s, software filters disabled, and 0.1 µV resolution. Preserve these header values without silently interpreting the 1000 Hz entry as an effective anti-alias cutoff. Our explicit resampling applies an additional anti-alias filter.

## Calibration-only quality audit adjustment (before fitting)

The first calibration block has large per-channel voltage offsets (verified against original int16 scaling), so applying a 120 µV artifact limit to absolute raw voltage would reject usable AC EEG solely for its offset. For both real-data branches assess amplitude, sample-step, and flatline limits on a separate fixed 1 Hz high-pass copy, retaining the original data for interpolation and each branch's feature filtering. Limits remain 120 µV and 60 µV/sample with a 2 s rejection guard. This is an acquisition/preprocessing correction based only on calibration signal quality, not classifier performance. Synthetic defaults remain unchanged.

EEG-only amplitude rules do not reliably remove moderate eye or muscle artifacts. HEOG/VEOG are retained for a held-out diagnostic and an EOG-only discrimination control; neither changes EEG model fitting or selection. No behavioral-correctness filtering is applied because response logs are outside this first download; all documented target/non-target trials are evaluated subject to signal-quality exclusions. This is not an exact replication of the authors' ERP analysis.

## Artifact-calibration correction (still before held-out scoring)

The first training attempt failed before fitting: quality-mask expansion left no usable rest baseline and essentially no calibration epochs across all three sessions. Calibration-only inspection showed repeated voltage excursions, not a marker/class issue. A separate pre-task segment is available before every session's first block context. Fit a two-channel linear EOG regression there (from recording second 2 to 14 s before the first task marker, bandpass 1–30 Hz, discard 2 s at each edge, ridge = 0.001 × mean EOG covariance diagonal). Freeze this projection and subtract its estimated eye contribution from all later EEG blocks. This artifact-calibration segment shares no samples with labeled calibration, validation, or test blocks.

Assess quality on a 1–30 Hz copy, matching the analyzed frequency range, so out-of-band sample steps do not independently invalidate all epochs. Amplitude/step thresholds and 2 s guard remain unchanged. Preserve the original data and all projection coefficients in the acquisition audit. EOG regression can remove eye-correlated neural activity as well, so it is a preprocessing assumption, not proof of clean cortical signals. Keep the EOG-only discrimination control. No held-out model scores were available when these changes were chosen.
